components.name: registry-scope
components.description: A URI fragment prefix such as //registry.example.test/ followed by a colon, scoping the setting to a registry host and optional path.

components.name: setting
components.description: _auth, _authToken, username, _password, email, cafile, certfile or keyfile.

components.name: value
components.description: A literal, a ${VARIABLE_NAME} reference or, for cafile/certfile/keyfile, a file path.

claims.statement: npm configuration files are ini-formatted key = value lists; environment variables can be replaced using ${VARIABLE_NAME}, and an undefined variable is left unreplaced unless the name is followed by a question mark, which forces an empty string.

sources.supports: All npm config files are an ini-formatted list of key = value parameters. Environment variables can be replaced using ${VARIABLE_NAME}. By default if the variable is not defined, it is left unreplaced. By adding ? after variable name they can be forced to evaluate to an empty string instead.

claims.statement: The settings _auth (base64 authentication string), _authToken (authentication token), username, _password and email, and the file-path settings cafile, certfile and keyfile, are the auth related configuration; the first six "must all be scoped to a specific registry" by a URI fragment prefix, which "ensures that npm will never send credentials to the wrong host".

sources.supports: The settings _auth, _authToken, username, _password, certfile, and keyfile must all be scoped to a specific registry. This ensures that npm will never send credentials to the wrong host. _auth (base64 authentication string), _authToken (authentication token), username, _password, email, cafile (path to certificate authority file), certfile (path to certificate file), keyfile (path to key file).

claims.statement: The page's examples place the token after a scoped key in the form //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken = MYTOKEN, with MYTOKEN a placeholder, and show that a path-scoped key applies to a single organization.

sources.locator: section: Custom / third-party config keys (good config example)

claims.statement: The page lists username and email beside the credential settings and gives no statement of their confidentiality; it lists _password and says nothing about its encoding or content.

sources.supports: username, _password, email are listed as auth related settings; no description of their confidentiality or encoding.

openQuestions.question: Does the npm documentation anywhere state what _password holds (a base64-encoded password?) and whether username is confidential?
